answer_text: Large language models are increasingly adopted to support scientific literature reviews and evidence synthesis, yet they frequently generate plausible-sounding but fabricated bibliographic references that require post-hoc verification [arXiv:2603.07287, стр. 1]. To prevent such fabrications during related work generation, modular toolkits like LitLLM apply Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and sentence-based planning to ground synthesized summaries directly in retrieved academic papers [arXiv:2402.01788, стр. 1]. Because retrieval systems and step-by-step reasoning prompts do not validate extracted findings across a broader research corpus, Peer Context Outlier Detection (P-COD) clusters methodologically similar papers in a shared semantic embedding space to flag anomalous data extractions for human review [arXiv:2604.01461, стр. 1]. Complementing claim-level verification, retrieval-grounded pipelines such as CiteCheck query scholarly metadata services to classify and automatically correct hallucinated or corrupted citations in AI-generated scientific reports [arXiv:2605.27700, стр. 2]. Additionally, open-source verification interfaces like CheckIfExist enable researchers to batch-validate compiled bibliographies and replace unverified LLM outputs with authenticated BibTeX and APA records prior to manuscript submission [arXiv:2602.15871, стр. 1].

Automated evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines relies heavily on LLM-as-a-judge frameworks to reduce the need for costly human annotations [arXiv:2311.09476, стр. 2]. Early reference-free frameworks such as RAGAS introduced prompt-based LLM evaluation to estimate faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance without requiring ground-truth reference answers [arXiv:2309.15217, стр. 2]. To improve adaptability across diverse domains and provide statistical guarantees, the ARES framework fine-tunes lightweight LLM judges on synthetically generated query-passage-answer triples and computes confidence intervals via prediction-powered inference [arXiv:2311.09476, стр. 1]. Moving beyond coarse holistic scores, RAGChecker decomposes generated responses and retrieved chunks into fine-grained claim-level entailment checks to diagnose specific retriever and generator failure modes [arXiv:2408.08067, стр. 1]. Similarly, enterprise-focused frameworks enforce structured rubric scoring over multi-turn histories and case metadata to expose operational failures like workflow misalignment [arXiv:2602.20379, стр. 1]. Despite these advances, recent surveys highlight that deploying LLMs as evaluative judges still faces standardization challenges regarding grading scales, prompt sensitivity, and alignment with human judgment [arXiv:2405.07437, стр. 13].

Autonomous large language model (LLM) agents are highly vulnerable to indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks, in which adversaries embed malicious directives inside untrusted external data returned by tools to hijack execution [arXiv:2603.10749, стр. 1]. An empirical study across 1.2 billion URLs revealed that in-page prompt injection is already deployed at scale on the web, identifying 15.3K confirmed instances across 11.7K webpages where 54 reusable templates account for 95% of all cases [arXiv:2604.27202, стр. 1]. To systematically evaluate how agents handle these threats in dynamic tool-calling environments, the AgentDojo framework provides a benchmark suite initially populated with 97 realistic tasks and 629 security test cases [arXiv:2406.13352, стр. 1]. At the model level, defensive training methods like SecAlign apply preference optimization to bolster robustness against unseen prompt injections while maintaining practical utility comparable to unaligned models [arXiv:2410.05451, стр. 1]. Because model-level alignment alone cannot guarantee structural constraints, system-level architectures such as the f-secure LLM system separate the LLM-based planner from a rule-based executor and apply information flow control principles to prevent execution trace compromise [arXiv:2409.19091, стр. 2]. Similarly, multi-layered defense frameworks combine content filtering, prompt architecture improvements, and response verification to protect retrieval-augmented agents across multiple pipeline stages [arXiv:2511.15759, стр. 2]. More recently, action-level causal attribution via AttriGuard leverages parallel counterfactual tests to gate proposed tool calls, achieving a 0% attack success rate under static attacks while remaining resilient against adaptive optimization-based adversaries [arXiv:2603.10749, стр. 2].

LangGraph has become the most widely adopted graph-based agent framework for complex tasks, functioning as a semi-deterministic multi-ready-unit scheduler that supports parallel node execution via fan-out/fan-in patterns, conditional edges, state channels, and runtime graph modification [arXiv:2604.11378, стр. 4]. Within this architecture, developers orchestrate multi-agent systems by explicitly defining states, agent nodes, and transition edges, as well as setting human-in-the-loop breakpoints during the graph execution process to guide complex workflows [arXiv:2412.03801, стр. 3]. In complex code synthesis and verification reasoning tasks such as microservice generation, multi-agent systems built on top of LangGraph divide responsibilities across specialized initialization, coding, and Docker testing nodes that rely on iterative reflection to improve output quality [arXiv:2508.20119, стр. 7]. Similarly, automated software debugging workflows utilize LangGraph as a graph-based orchestration library to coordinate LLM-based agent operations, significantly enhancing both the efficiency and accuracy of bug fixing [arXiv:2502.18465, стр. 3]. Empirical benchmark evaluations of multi-agent assistant workflows further show that because LangGraph passes only the system prompt and prior agent results as input, it achieves highly competitive token efficiency at an average cost of $0.14 per query compared to $0.80 in AutoGen [arXiv:2504.18373, стр. 5].

Iterative self-refinement enables language agents to generate an initial output, produce multi-aspect feedback on that response, and iteratively refine their generation using the same underlying model without additional training [arXiv:2303.17651, стр. 2]. Extending this paradigm to multi-trial agentic settings, the Reflexion framework converts binary or scalar reward signals from task trajectories into verbal self-reflections stored in an episodic memory buffer to guide future trials [arXiv:2303.11366, стр. 2]. In complex planning domains, Language Agent Tree Search unifies reasoning, acting, and planning by combining Monte Carlo Tree Search with both environmental observations and verbal self-reflection to refine decision-making [arXiv:2310.04406, стр. 2]. Despite the popularity of reflection loops, empirical evaluations of intrinsic self-correction demonstrate that large language models struggle to properly judge the correctness of their own reasoning without external feedback, often degrading performance by modifying correct answers into incorrect ones [arXiv:2310.01798, стр. 2]. To overcome the limitations of purely internal reflection, the CRITIC framework equips agents to interact with external tools such as search engines and code interpreters to verify desired aspects of an initial output before amending errors based on grounded critiques [arXiv:2305.11738, стр. 1].

Standard retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems rely on splitting text documents into isolated chunks and embedding them into a vector space to perform semantic similarity search [arXiv:2404.16130, стр. 3]. While this vector-based semantic retrieval excels at answering detailed, single-hop factual queries, it struggles to connect dispersed information across documents when answering complex, multi-hop questions [arXiv:2502.11371, стр. 1]. To overcome these structural limitations, GraphRAG constructs a knowledge graph of entities and relationships from the source corpus, enabling the retrieval of interconnected subgraphs or hierarchical community summaries [arXiv:2405.16506, стр. 2]. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that GraphRAG significantly outperforms naive vector search in answer comprehensiveness and diversity on global sensemaking and multi-hop reasoning tasks [arXiv:2404.16130, стр. 1]. In domain-specific document question answering, GraphRAG achieves higher context precision and faithfulness by following explicit relational paths, whereas traditional vector retrieval maintains higher context recall for direct extractive queries [arXiv:2408.04948, стр. 6]. Consequently, modern architectures such as LightRAG and HybridRAG integrate graph-based indexing with vector similarity search to balance relational reasoning depth, retrieval efficiency, and fine-grained factual recall [arXiv:2410.05779, стр. 1].

Reducing the monetary overhead of deploying large language models (LLMs) relies heavily on dynamic API routing and cost-aware external tool execution [arXiv:2305.05176, стр. 1]. Foundational frameworks like FrugalGPT address API pricing disparities by utilizing sequential LLM cascades that query inexpensive models first and escalate to costly proprietary APIs only when response reliability scores are insufficient [arXiv:2305.05176, стр. 2]. Rather than invoking multiple models sequentially, predictive routing systems such as RouteLLM leverage human preference data and matrix factorization to estimate ahead of inference whether a weaker model can satisfy a prompt, cutting expensive strong-model calls by more than half [arXiv:2406.18665, стр. 7]. Expanding beyond binary selection, Cost-Spectrum Contrastive Routing (CSCR) embeds user queries and diverse API experts into a shared metric space to execute microsecond nearest-neighbor routing that optimizes the accuracy-cost Pareto frontier by up to 25% [arXiv:2508.12491, стр. 1]. For classification-oriented workloads, ThriftLLM formalizes budget-constrained model selection as a dynamic programming problem to aggregate responses from an optimal subset of candidate APIs without exceeding user-defined financial limits [arXiv:2501.04901, стр. 1]. When LLMs are augmented with external APIs and functional tools, CATP-LLM mitigates multi-step execution costs by integrating cost-aware offline planning with fine-tuned compact backbones that outperform GPT-4 in plan quality at a fraction of the expense [arXiv:2411.16313, стр. 1]. Furthermore, the BATS framework formalizes test-time scaling for tool-augmented agents under strict invocation budgets, unifying token consumption and third-party API fees into a single economic metric to prevent wasteful search and browsing loops [arXiv:2511.17006, стр. 2].

Lifelong learning agents require specialized memory architectures to accumulate knowledge across sequential tasks while mitigating catastrophic forgetting [arXiv:2503.12923, стр. 1]. To overcome finite context windows, operating-system-inspired frameworks such as MemGPT manage hierarchical memory tiers to provide an illusion of unlimited context during extended interactions [arXiv:2310.08560, стр. 1]. In continual visual learning, the Remembering Transformer incorporates a mixture-of-adapters architecture alongside generative novelty detection to dynamically route task data and preserve prior knowledge with minimal memory overhead [arXiv:2404.07518, стр. 1]. Furthermore, transformer attention mechanisms naturally develop human-like episodic memory structures and temporal contiguity effects during training, which supports processing over extended temporal contexts [arXiv:2502.06902, стр. 1]. For inter-environment lifelong learning, frameworks like LifeMem cluster interaction trajectories into structured workflows and distill reusable skills to enable cross-domain experience transfer [arXiv:2609.12655, стр. 1]. Together, cognitive architectures and large language models can be integrated to verify, update, and store domain-specific production rules for long-term autonomous adaptation [arXiv:2403.00810, стр. 1].

Automated red teaming uses attacker language models to automatically generate adversarial test cases and uncover harmful behaviors in target models before deployment [arXiv:2202.03286, стр. 1]. In black-box settings, Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement (PAIR) leverages an attacker LLM to iteratively refine semantic jailbreak prompts against a target LLM in fewer than twenty queries [arXiv:2310.08419, стр. 1]. Standardized evaluation frameworks such as HarmBench benchmark both automated red-teaming attacks and robust refusal mechanisms across 510 unique harmful behaviors spanning textual and multimodal domains [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 1]. Autonomous multi-agent frameworks like AutoRedTeamer further expand vulnerability discovery by integrating lifelong attack discovery with automated strategy orchestration [arXiv:2503.15754, стр. 1]. To detect and block adversarial inputs and unsafe generations in conversational applications, safeguard models such as Llama Guard classify user prompts and model responses according to a safety risk taxonomy [arXiv:2312.06674, стр. 1]. Complementing classifier-based guards, SmoothLLM detects and mitigates gradient-based and semantic jailbreaks by applying random character-level perturbations to multiple copies of an input prompt and aggregating the resulting predictions [arXiv:2310.03684, стр. 1].

Traditional text-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines rely on optical character recognition and layout parsing, which frequently discard crucial visual information embedded within complex tables, charts, and figures in scientific documents [arXiv:2406.11251, стр. 1]. To overcome cascading parsing errors, recent multimodal retrieval architectures bypass text extraction entirely by encoding rendered document page screenshots directly through vision-language models [arXiv:2406.11251, стр. 2]. Specifically, the ColPali framework generates multi-vector patch embeddings from page images and employs a late-interaction matching mechanism to substantially improve retrieval accuracy and latency across visually complex pages [arXiv:2407.01449, стр. 2]. Building upon visual page retrievers, end-to-end multimodal RAG systems like VisRAG utilize vision-language models for both dense page retrieval and visual answer generation, effectively preserving intricate tabular layouts and graphical plots [arXiv:2410.10594, стр. 3]. Similarly, M3DocRAG combines ColPali visual embeddings with multimodal language models to synthesize evidence across multi-page and multi-document corpora containing diverse figures, charts, and tables [arXiv:2411.04952, стр. 3]. Despite these architectural advances, the SPIQA benchmark demonstrates that answering fine-grained questions over scientific articles still requires integrating multiple visual contexts with accompanying text, where retrieval filtering errors remain a key bottleneck [arXiv:2407.09413, стр. 1]. Furthermore, evaluations on long-context scientific and technical documents in MMLongBench-Doc confirm that cross-page reasoning over heterogeneous tables and figures continues to challenge current multimodal pipelines [arXiv:2407.01523, стр. 2].

The rapid adoption of large language models in scientific writing has resulted in a marked surge of fabricated references across repositories, highlighting the vulnerability of automated academic synthesis to hallucinatory outputs [arXiv:2605.07723, стр. 1]. Large-scale empirical evaluations demonstrate that non-existent and misattributed citations remain an unavoidable challenge across major foundation models when generating reference lists and synthesizing literature [arXiv:2412.13612, стр. 2]. To systematically address these failures, recent taxonomies categorize errors into knowledge-based and logic-based hallucinations, demonstrating that retrieval grounding and reasoning enhancements serve as complementary mitigation mechanisms [arXiv:2510.24476, стр. 1]. In literature synthesis tasks, decomposing the workflow into explicit retrieval and plan-conditioned generation steps suppresses hallucinated references by 18% to 26% relative to direct prompting [arXiv:2412.15249, стр. 1]. Standard retrieval-augmented systems nonetheless remain vulnerable when retrieved evidence is incomplete, as per-document prompting lacks the corpus-wide awareness needed to detect inconsistent scientific claims [arXiv:2604.01461, стр. 2]. Comparing extracted findings against semantic peer groups enables context-aware outlier detection, achieving up to 98% precision in identifying corrupted facts and filtering out hallucinations from automated scientific literature reviews [arXiv:2604.01461, стр. 1].

Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems requires assessing both the retrieval and generation stages without relying solely on static ground-truth answers [arXiv:2309.15217, стр. 2]. The Ragas framework establishes an automated approach by prompting language models to decompose outputs and calculate reference-free metrics such as faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance [arXiv:2309.15217, стр. 2]. To improve evaluation reliability beyond heuristic prompting, the ARES system fine-tunes domain-specific LLM judges and incorporates prediction-powered inference to provide statistical confidence intervals over system rankings [arXiv:2311.09476, стр. 1]. Moving beyond coarse response-level scoring, RAGChecker introduces claim-level entailment checking to conduct fine-grained diagnostic evaluations across both the retriever and generator modules [arXiv:2408.08067, стр. 1]. Furthermore, recent methodologies like ConsJudge address inherent evaluator biases by leveraging LLM judge consistency across multiple evaluation aspects to select more accurate and aligned judgment models [arXiv:2502.18817, стр. 2].

Autonomous agents driven by large language models (LLMs) face severe security threats from indirect prompt injection, where adversaries embed unvetted instructions inside external retrieved data to hijack execution flow [arXiv:2302.12173, стр. 1]. Because standard agent architectures conflate instructional commands with passive contextual data, models struggle to recognize instruction provenance across environment interactions [arXiv:2312.14197, стр. 2]. Empirical evaluations on tool-integrated agent benchmarks demonstrate that advanced commercial and open-weight models frequently execute unauthorized downstream actions when triggered by poisoned tool returns [arXiv:2403.02691, стр. 2]. To counter this vulnerability, input transformation techniques such as spotlighting use structured delimiting and data marking to emphasize content provenance and suppress embedded commands [arXiv:2403.14720, стр. 1]. Complementary runtime frameworks introduce intermediate security layers, including external prompt-injection detectors and tool filtering, to inspect outputs and restrict access to unauthorized APIs [arXiv:2406.13352, стр. 8]. However, dynamic benchmarks reveal that while isolated guardrails substantially lower attack success rates, maintaining robust security without sacrificing benign task utility remains an open challenge against adaptive adversaries [arXiv:2406.13352, стр. 1].

Modern multi-agent architectures increasingly leverage graph-based orchestration to address complex reasoning problems by decomposing monolithic workflows into modular, state-aware processing units [arXiv:2509.25693, стр. 2]. Unlike rigid static pipelines, graph-based frameworks such as LangGraph represent individual agents and specialized tools as nodes while directing control flow through state-dependent edges, allowing for dynamic branching, iterative refinement, and runtime adaptation [arXiv:2509.25693, стр. 2]. In complex reasoning tasks, coordinating agents through cyclical feedback loops and structured state persistence significantly enhances tool invocation accuracy and reduces error propagation compared to unconstrained conversational architectures [arXiv:2411.18241, стр. 2]. Furthermore, integrating explicit graph schemas with supervisory orchestrators enables dynamic role delegation and robust intermediate context management across extended reasoning trajectories [arXiv:2509.25693, стр. 2]. By constraining agent interactions through inspectable graph topologies and shared memory states, systems can systematically prevent infinite loops and improve fault tolerance during complex multi-step inference [arXiv:2411.18241, стр. 2]. Comparative benchmarking across multi-agent platforms demonstrates that graph-structured routing and centralized state sharing also provide notable efficiency advantages, maintaining manageable computational costs during multi-turn orchestration [arXiv:2504.18373, стр. 5].

Self-correction and automated feedback mechanisms have emerged as vital paradigms enabling large language models to iteratively evaluate and refine their outputs without continuous human intervention. [arXiv:2308.03188, стр. 1] The Self-Refine framework operationalizes this concept by employing the same underlying language model to generate feedback on its own initial draft and subsequently refine the text through multi-turn iteration. [arXiv:2303.17651, стр. 2] Extending iterative refinement to autonomous agents, the Reflexion architecture utilizes verbal reinforcement learning by storing linguistic evaluative reflections in an episodic memory buffer across successive attempts. [arXiv:2303.11366, стр. 2] To mitigate the hallucination and unreliability inherent in purely internal self-assessment, the CRITIC framework introduces tool-interactive critiquing where models verify outputs against external sources such as web search engines and code interpreters before revising. [arXiv:2305.11738, стр. 2] Despite these advancements, rigorous evaluations demonstrate that models struggle with intrinsic self-correction on complex reasoning tasks in the absence of external ground-truth signals, frequently degrading performance by revising originally correct solutions into incorrect ones. [arXiv:2310.01798, стр. 1]

Traditional retrieval-augmented generation relies on dense semantic vector search over text chunks, which frequently fails to answer global sensemaking questions that require synthesizing insights across an entire document corpus [arXiv:2404.16130, стр. 1]. Unlike standard semantic search that retrieves text purely based on surface embedding similarity, GraphRAG structures external document knowledge into interconnected nodes, edges, and communities to preserve relational context [arXiv:2408.08921, стр. 2]. Standard vector retrieval also struggles in multi-hop question answering scenarios where associative chains between disparate passages must be discovered and traversed [arXiv:2405.14831, стр. 1]. Empirical comparisons demonstrate that hierarchical community-based retrieval significantly outperforms baseline vector search in both response comprehensiveness and diversity on corpus-wide queries [arXiv:2404.16130, стр. 7]. Furthermore, dual-level graph indexing that jointly captures entity-level facts and macro-level themes allows graph-based retrieval to consistently surpass naive chunk-based vector matching across varied knowledge domains [arXiv:2410.05779, стр. 5].

Recent research addresses the significant inference overhead of frontier models by orchestrating queries across heterogeneous model tiers using cascades and dynamic routers [arXiv:2305.05176, стр. 1]. In cascaded architectures such as FrugalGPT, an adaptive router forwards incoming requests to cheaper models first and only falls back to more expensive services if generation confidence falls below a threshold [arXiv:2305.05176, стр. 5]. To prevent multi-round cascade latency, preference-based routers such as RouteLLM use predictive scoring heads to dispatch queries directly between cheap and frontier models according to an explicit cost-quality threshold [arXiv:2406.18665, стр. 2]. Beyond model selection, scaling tool-augmented agents to massive API libraries requires cost-effective retrieval and routing mechanisms to avoid stuffing thousands of parameter schemas into context windows [arXiv:2307.16789, стр. 1]. Integrating neural retrievers into tool frameworks like ToolLLM allows agents to select only relevant API definitions prior to execution, mitigating unnecessary token expenditure [arXiv:2307.16789, стр. 3]. Furthermore, pairing retriever-aware models like Gorilla with document search allows language models to invoke accurate API calls while minimizing parameter hallucination and call volume [arXiv:2305.15334, стр. 2]. Finally, recent agent benchmarks incorporate unified cost functions accounting for both token consumption and external API invocation fees to optimize the Pareto frontier under hard execution budgets [arXiv:2511.17006, стр. 2].

Lifelong learning in large language model based agents relies on dedicated memory architectures to continuously accumulate, retain, and reuse knowledge across evolving tasks while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. [arXiv:2501.07278, стр. 1] To support coherent long-term behaviors, early generative agent architectures maintain an extensive memory stream of chronological observations retrieved through a combined score of recency, importance, and relevance. [arXiv:2304.03442, стр. 4] Beyond raw event logging, architectures like MemoryBank incorporate biologically inspired retention mechanisms grounded in the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve to update memory strength and discard obsolete details over time. [arXiv:2305.10250, стр. 3] To overcome finite context windows during indefinite deployment, hierarchical operating-system frameworks partition memory into active working context and persistent external recall storage managed through autonomous function calls. [arXiv:2310.08560, стр. 2] In open-ended embodied environments, lifelong learning agents construct persistent procedural memories by indexing newly synthesized and verified executable code within a vector database skill library. [arXiv:2305.16291, стр. 2] Complementing procedural and episodic stores, verbal reflection architectures maintain episodic self-evaluations that record natural language feedback from past execution failures to iteratively guide subsequent decision cycles. [arXiv:2303.11366, стр. 2]

Automated red teaming of large language models emerged prominently with gradient-based optimization methods that search for adversarial suffixes capable of bypassing model alignment safeguards [arXiv:2307.15043, стр. 1]. To address practical black-box settings where model weights are inaccessible, Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement (PAIR) uses an attacker language model to autonomously query and refine semantic jailbreak prompts [arXiv:2310.08419, стр. 2]. Expanding upon single-stream prompt refinement, Tree of Attacks with Pruning (TAP) organizes the attack space into a branching tree search that systematically prunes unpromising candidates [arXiv:2312.02119, стр. 2]. On the defensive front, randomized input perturbation strategies such as SmoothLLM mitigate adversarial exploits by detecting and aggregating responses across multiple perturbed copies of an incoming prompt [arXiv:2310.03684, стр. 1]. Complementing perturbation defenses, specialized moderation models like Llama Guard act as classifier layers designed to detect policy-violating prompts and outputs directly [arXiv:2312.06674, стр. 1]. To rigorously benchmark these adversarial attacks and safety defenses, standardized evaluation suites such as HarmBench provide automated pipelines and taxonomies to quantify red teaming efficacy and robust refusal performance [arXiv:2402.04249, стр. 1]

Scientific research papers are inherently multimodal artifacts where vital experimental findings, data distributions, and scientific workflows are concentrated within complex tables and figures [arXiv:2411.04075, стр. 1]. Conventional retrieval-augmented generation systems struggle to process such literature because standard optical character recognition and text-chunking pipelines discard essential spatial hierarchies, graphical structures, and layout geometry [arXiv:2407.01449, стр. 1]. To overcome these limitations, vision-language retrieval models embed full page screenshots directly into multi-vector representations, utilizing late-interaction operators to preserve fine-grained alignments between textual queries and visual components like charts or table cells [arXiv:2407.01449, стр. 4]. Comprehensive multimodal RAG frameworks systematically ingest heterogeneous modalities by parsing, indexing, and jointly reasoning over interleaved passages, tabular data, and visual graphics [arXiv:2510.03663, стр. 1]. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that decomposing documents into dedicated textual and visual representations prior to multimodal fusion yields substantially higher retrieval precision and answer faithfulness than text-only baselines [arXiv:2510.03663, стр. 2]. Finally, recent taxonomies emphasize that reliable scientific document understanding requires bridging the gap between dense visual representation and structured evidence synthesis across multi-page diagrams and data tables [arXiv:2510.15253, стр. 1].

Mitigating hallucination in LLM-based scientific literature review is crucial because ungrounded models can fabricate references; in OpenScholar’s experiments, GPT-4 produced fabricated citations in 78–90% of cases when asked to cite recent literature. \[arXiv:2411.14199, стр. 1]
Retrieval-augmented generation addresses this failure by grounding answers in external documents, and PaperQA applies it to full-text scientific articles while assessing the relevance of sources and passages. \[arXiv:2312.07559, стр. 1]
PaperQA2 strengthens this pipeline through iterative search, LLM reranking, contextual summarization, and answer generation from top-ranked evidence summaries, reducing the chance that irrelevant retrieved passages shape the review. \[arXiv:2409.13740, стр. 3]
Empirically, PaperQA reported no hallucinated citations among 237 references in its evaluation, although the authors note that citing an inaccessible secondary source could still introduce hallucination. \[arXiv:2312.07559, стр. 8]
Beyond retrieval, Chain-of-Verification reduces hallucination by drafting a response, generating fact-checking questions, answering them independently, and producing a revised final answer. \[arXiv:2309.11495, стр. 1]
SelfCheckGPT offers a complementary black-box detection method that samples multiple responses and identifies likely hallucinations through inconsistency, without requiring an external database. \[arXiv:2303.08896, стр. 2]
Finally, reliable review systems should be evaluated for both citation recall, measuring whether statements are supported by cited passages, and citation precision, identifying irrelevant citations, rather than for reference existence alone. \[arXiv:2305.14627, стр. 4]

LLM-as-a-judge provides a scalable and explainable approximation to costly human evaluation, with strong judges such as GPT-4 achieving over 80% agreement with human preferences on MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena. \[arXiv:2306.05685, стр. 1]
RAG evaluation is especially challenging because these systems combine retrieval and generation components while relying on dynamic knowledge sources, motivating multidimensional metrics such as relevance, accuracy, and faithfulness. \[arXiv:2405.07437, стр. 1]
RAGAS addresses this challenge through reference-free metrics that assess whether retrieved passages are relevant and focused, whether the generator uses them faithfully, and whether the resulting response is high quality, without requiring ground-truth human annotations. \[arXiv:2309.15217, стр. 1]
ARES instead fine-tunes lightweight language-model judges on synthetic data to score context relevance, answer faithfulness, and answer relevance, while using a small human-annotated dataset for prediction-powered inference to mitigate prediction errors. \[arXiv:2311.09476, стр. 1]
Moving beyond response-level scoring, RAGChecker uses claim-level entailment checking to produce diagnostic metrics for both retrieval and generation, and its meta-evaluation reports stronger correlations with human judgments than competing metrics. \[arXiv:2408.08067, стр. 1]
However, LLM judges are not neutral measurement instruments: GPT-4 and Llama 2 exhibit nontrivial self-recognition, and fine-tuning experiments reveal a linear correlation between self-recognition and self-preference bias. \[arXiv:2404.13076, стр. 1]
Consequently, research on reliable LLM-as-a-judge frameworks emphasizes consistency, bias mitigation, adaptation to diverse assessment scenarios, and explicit evaluation of evaluator reliability. \[arXiv:2411.15594, стр. 1]

Indirect prompt injection occurs when LLM-integrated agents retrieve attacker-controlled instructions embedded in external data, blurring the boundary between data and instructions and enabling remote control, data theft, and unauthorized API calls. \[arXiv:2302.12173, стр. 1]
AgentDojo provides an extensible benchmark comprising 97 realistic tasks and 629 security test cases for evaluating prompt-injection attacks and defenses in tool-using agents. \[arXiv:2406.13352, стр. 1]
Model-level defenses such as StruQ separate prompts from data and fine-tune LLMs to follow instructions only in the prompt channel, reducing tested manual attack success rates below 2% while remaining vulnerable to some optimization-based attacks. \[arXiv:2402.06363, стр. 2]
IsolateGPT instead isolates third-party applications in constrained execution environments and mediates their interactions through well-defined interfaces, reporting no loss of benchmark functionality and overhead below 30% for three-quarters of tested queries. \[arXiv:2403.04960, стр. 1]
CaMeL extracts control and data flows from trusted user queries and enforces capability-based security policies during tool calls, completing 77% of AgentDojo tasks with provable security compared with 84% for an undefended system. \[arXiv:2503.18813, стр. 1]
Progent enforces least privilege through deterministic symbolic policies over tool calls and SMT-checked policy updates, reducing attack success on AgentDojo from 39.9% to 1.0% while maintaining utility. \[arXiv:2504.11703, стр. 2]
Nevertheless, AgentDojo’s authors caution that significant breakthroughs in distinguishing instructions from data will likely be necessary to resist stronger adaptive attacks. \[arXiv:2406.13352, стр. 2]

Research on LLM-based multi-agent systems frames complex reasoning as coordinated task distribution, knowledge sharing, and subtask execution among specialized agents pursuing shared objectives. \[arXiv:2501.06322, стр. 2] Within this landscape, LangGraph supports stateful multi-actor workflows with fine-grained state control, cycles, branching, persistence, and human-in-the-loop intervention. \[arXiv:2503.13415, стр. 41] Wang and Duan’s machine-translation implementation illustrates this abstraction concretely: states, nodes, and edges define the workflow, while an intent agent routes inputs to specialized language agents. \[arXiv:2412.03801, стр. 7] For complex and ambiguous problems, Rasal and Hauer’s orchestration approach decomposes tasks into manageable subproblems, assigns them to specialized LLM agents or non-LLM functions for parallel resolution, and synthesizes the outputs into a comprehensive answer. \[arXiv:2402.16713, стр. 1] Complementary work by Du et al. shows that repeated proposal, critique, and revision across debating model instances improves mathematical and strategic reasoning as well as factual validity. \[arXiv:2305.14325, стр. 1] RECONCILE extends consensus-based collaboration through diverse models, multiple discussion rounds, and confidence-weighted voting, reporting gains of up to 11.4% over prior single-agent and multi-agent baselines across seven benchmarks. \[arXiv:2309.13007, стр. 1] These findings suggest that LangGraph implementations should combine graph-based orchestration with explicit output validation, because multi-agent coordination increases complexity and erroneous agent outputs can cascade into compounding mistakes. \[arXiv:2501.06322, стр. 6]

ReAct established an early foundation for agentic self-correction by interleaving reasoning traces with task-specific actions, enabling agents to update plans, handle exceptions, and gather external information during execution. \[arXiv:2210.03629, стр. 1]
Reflexion extended this approach across trials by converting task feedback into verbal reflections stored in episodic memory, improving subsequent decision-making without updating model weights. \[arXiv:2303.11366, стр. 1]
Self-Refine demonstrated a training-free alternative in which the same language model generates an output, critiques it, and iteratively revises it, producing improvements across seven diverse tasks. \[arXiv:2303.17651, стр. 1]
CRITIC highlighted the limitations of purely internal critique by using external tools to validate and progressively amend outputs, finding that self-correction without external feedback can yield modest gains or even degrade performance. \[arXiv:2305.11738, стр. 2]
Tree of Thoughts complements output-level revision with deliberate search over intermediate thoughts, using language-model self-evaluation to select reasoning paths and look ahead or backtrack when necessary. \[arXiv:2305.10601, стр. 1]

Standard semantic-search RAG segments documents into chunks, embeds chunks and queries in a shared vector space, and supplies the most similar chunks to the answer generator. \[arXiv:2502.11371, стр. 3]
This approach works well when answers are localized in a few passages, but it struggles with corpus-wide sensemaking questions that require synthesizing connections across the entire document collection. \[arXiv:2404.16130, стр. 2]
The original GraphRAG design instead constructs an entity–relationship knowledge graph, partitions it into hierarchical communities, generates community summaries, and combines partial answers through map-reduce processing. \[arXiv:2404.16130, стр. 2]
For global sensemaking questions over million-token-scale corpora, its authors report substantial improvements in answer comprehensiveness and diversity over conventional RAG. \[arXiv:2404.16130, стр. 1]
However, a broader controlled evaluation finds that standard RAG excels on detailed single-hop queries, whereas HippoRAG2 and local community-based GraphRAG perform best on the tested multi-hop benchmarks. \[arXiv:2502.11371, стр. 4]
The same study cautions that global community search can discard fine-grained evidence, while incomplete knowledge graphs may omit answer-critical entities and relations. \[arXiv:2502.11371, стр. 4]
These findings motivate query-dependent selection or integration of both approaches rather than treating GraphRAG as a universal replacement, with graph-construction cost, noise, and system efficiency included in the design trade-off. \[arXiv:2502.11371, стр. 8]

Gorilla established retrieval-augmented API selection as a way to improve API-call accuracy, adapt to documentation changes, and reduce hallucination. \[arXiv:2305.15334, стр. 1]
ToolLLM extended this line to 16,464 real-world RESTful APIs, pairing a neural API retriever with depth-first search-based decision trees for complex, multi-tool instructions. \[arXiv:2307.16789, стр. 1]
For cost reduction at the tool layer, LATM assigns one-time tool creation to GPT-4 and repeated tool use to GPT-3.5, reporting GPT-4-level performance at significantly lower inference cost. \[arXiv:2305.17126, стр. 1]
EcoAssistant combines iterative code execution, cheaper-to-stronger LLM escalation, and retrieval of successful past solutions for code-driven API queries, exceeding GPT-4’s success rate by 10 points while using less than half its cost. \[arXiv:2310.03046, стр. 1]
At the model-routing layer, FrugalGPT learns query-specific LLM cascades and reports up to 98% cost reduction while matching the best individual model, or a 4% accuracy improvement over GPT-4 at equal cost. \[arXiv:2305.05176, стр. 1]
RouteLLM offers a complementary approach, training on human preference data to route queries between stronger and weaker LLMs and achieving over twofold cost savings without sacrificing response quality. \[arXiv:2406.18665, стр. 1]
Finally, BATS makes tool-call budgets explicit and jointly accounts for token and tool consumption, showing that budget-aware planning and verification improve the cost–performance frontier rather than merely increasing tool calls. \[arXiv:2511.17006, стр. 1]

CoALA organizes agent memory into short-term working memory and long-term episodic, semantic, and procedural stores, providing a useful taxonomy for lifelong-agent design. \[arXiv:2309.02427, стр. 9] Generative Agents implements episodic retention as a natural-language memory stream, combining recency, importance, and relevance for retrieval while reflection synthesizes experiences into higher-level inferences. \[arXiv:2304.03442, стр. 2] MemoryBank complements retrieval with an Ebbinghaus-inspired updating mechanism that forgets or reinforces memories according to elapsed time and significance, supporting adaptation during sustained interactions. \[arXiv:2305.10250, стр. 1] MemGPT instead adopts an operating-system analogy, using function calls to page information between a bounded main context and external storage. \[arXiv:2310.08560, стр. 1] Whereas these systems emphasize knowledge retention, Voyager demonstrates procedural lifelong memory through an ever-growing library of executable skills whose compositional reuse alleviates catastrophic forgetting and supports transfer to new Minecraft worlds. \[arXiv:2305.16291, стр. 1] A-MEM further makes memory organization adaptive by constructing structured notes, generating links to related memories, and updating existing representations as new experiences arrive, rather than relying on predetermined memory operations. \[arXiv:2502.12110, стр. 2]

Early automated red teaming moved beyond hand-written tests by using language models to generate cases and classifiers to identify failures, uncovering tens of thousands of offensive replies from a 280B-parameter chatbot. \[arXiv:2202.03286, стр. 1]
GPTFuzzer subsequently adapted software fuzzing to black-box red teaming by mutating human-written seed templates, selecting promising variants, and employing a judgment model to assess jailbreak success. \[arXiv:2309.10253, стр. 1]
PAIR introduced iterative attacker–target interaction, enabling an attacker LLM to refine semantic jailbreaks without human intervention and often succeed within twenty target queries. \[arXiv:2310.08419, стр. 1]
TAP extended this iterative paradigm with tree-based exploration and evaluator-guided pruning, reporting jailbreaks for more than 80% of tested prompts against models including GPT-4-Turbo and GPT-4o. \[arXiv:2312.02119, стр. 1]
AutoDAN complicated detection by using a hierarchical genetic algorithm to generate semantically meaningful jailbreak prompts capable of bypassing perplexity-based defenses. \[arXiv:2310.04451, стр. 1]
On the defensive side, JailGuard detects jailbreak and hijacking attacks across text and image modalities by mutating untrusted inputs and measuring discrepancies among the resulting model responses. \[arXiv:2312.10766, стр. 1]
In contrast, GradSafe identifies jailbreak prompts through similar loss-gradient patterns in safety-critical parameters when prompts are paired with compliance responses, achieving detection on Llama-2 without further training. \[arXiv:2402.13494, стр. 1]

Scientific-document RAG must jointly reason over prose, figures, and tables; SPIQA formalizes this challenge with 270K questions and a chain-of-thought evaluation using in-context retrieval over computer-science papers. \[arXiv:2407.09413, стр. 1]
One major design avoids brittle text extraction: ColPali embeds document-page images into multi-vector representations and applies late-interaction matching, outperforming text-centric retrieval pipelines on ViDoRe. \[arXiv:2407.01449, стр. 1]
VisRAG extends this vision-centric approach to end-to-end generation by retrieving VLM-embedded document images for a VLM generator, reporting 20–40% end-to-end gains over traditional text-based RAG. \[arXiv:2410.10594, стр. 1]
For evidence distributed across pages and documents, M3DocRAG combines multimodal retrieval with a multimodal language model to support open- and closed-domain, single- and multi-hop question answering while preserving visual information. \[arXiv:2411.04952, стр. 1]
An alternative scientific-document pipeline converts tables and figures into VLM-generated textual summaries, then combines semantic and lexical retrieval through reciprocal-rank fusion and cross-encoder reranking, reporting a 157% retrieval-quality improvement over naive RAG with 50 ms of additional latency. \[arXiv:2607.24799, стр. 1]
Nevertheless, MMDocRAG’s 4,055 expert-annotated question–answer pairs and evaluation of 60 language or vision-language models with 14 retrieval systems reveal persistent difficulties in multimodal evidence retrieval, selection, and integration, making reliable evidence grounding a central open problem. \[arXiv:2505.16470, стр. 1]
